game.name: Balatro
game.short_description: The poker roguelike. Balatro is a hypnotically satisfying deckbuilder where you play illegal poker hands, discover game-changing jokers, and trigger adrenaline-pumping, outrageous combos.

commentary.label: Tier list Part 2 (2024)
commentary.summary: Balatro is a solo-developed poker-themed deck-building roguelike that exploded in popularity seemingly out of nowhere. He argues the hype is justified: it is extremely simple to understand yet strategically deep, and it is intensely satisfying thanks to multiplicative score scaling. He recommends it to nearly anyone and places it in S tier. His main reservation is that it is currently unbalanced, though a joker-rebalancing update was imminent.
praise: Among the simplest deck builders: few keywords, quick poker tutorial, no poker knowledge needed
Simple mechanics combined with deep strategy, which he sees as the best kind of design
Extremely satisfying multiplicative combos and huge exploding numbers
Fast deck changes, frequent discards, and quick access to jokers make every run differ early
Rewards game-breaking builds without making them trivial, since you must understand the mechanics
Normal difficulty goes effectively infinite so you can keep scaling until the game catches up
Quick-paced runs that are easy to restart over and over
criticism: Currently pretty unbalanced, with lots of tweaking still possible
Some runs feel normal and unremarkable unless you find and plan around a build
Score beyond the target gives no extra reward, so huge numbers are purely for fun
unique_points: Poker hands as the core deck-building twist, making it approachable to anyone
Exponential multiplier scaling as a central satisfaction engine
Endless mode on normal difficulty means players chase breaking the game rather than higher difficulties
Design lesson: approachability plus strategic depth drove its broad appeal
commentary.quote: it's one of the easier games out there to break and yet still feel rewarding
design_criteria: Simplicity and approachability: few keywords, easy onboarding for any audience
Strategic depth: easy to learn but hard to master
Satisfaction/feel: multiplicative combos and big numbers
Synergies and build diversity: jokers and deck changes create varied runs
Run length and pacing: fast runs with quick deck churn keep replays fresh
Difficulty scaling: infinite normal mode rewards game-breaking
Risk vs reward: breaking the game is rewarding but requires mechanical understanding

commentary.label: Top 10 of 2024 (#1)
commentary.summary: Balatro is a poker-based deck-building roguelike where you play poker hands to beat score targets across eight antes, modifying your deck, upgrading hands and collecting Jokers. He calls it simple to learn but hard to master, and names it his favorite roguelike of the year, placing it at number one. He especially values the variety of builds, the earned feeling of a powerful run, and a well-balanced endless mode with huge numbers.
praise: Simple mechanics with deep strategy, which he sees as the foundation of a great strategy roguelike
Every Joker is unique, enabling many builds so runs feel different from each other
Powerful builds feel earned through knowledge and timing, like in The Binding of Isaac
Endless mode is enjoyable and addicting, and achievements still unlock there
Exponential score growth is implemented well and stays balanced despite many ways to multiply points
Audio-visual feedback is very satisfying: the point-counting sound and the score catching fire at high numbers
Varied starting decks and difficulty options give replayability and challenge
criticism: Reaching huge scores requires luck plus a lot of game knowledge
Not every run ends in a monstrous build, though he says the gameplay remains fun regardless
unique_points: Poker deck-builder hybrid where Jokers act as passive abilities driving build variety
Exponential growth is notoriously hard to balance in roguelikes, yet Balatro handles it better than anything he has seen
Endless mode that is genuinely fun, with achievements still unlockable
commentary.quote: this is my favorite rogl I've played this year
design_criteria: Simplicity vs depth: easy to understand, hard to master
Build diversity: unique Jokers give a wide range of strategies
Synergies and scaling: exponential growth balanced well
Earned power fantasy: overpowered runs feel earned by knowledge
Endless mode: enjoyable and keeps achievements active
Audio/visual feedback: satisfying counting sound and flaming score
Replayability: varied starting decks and difficulty options

community.one_liner: A poker-themed roguelike deckbuilder by solo dev LocalThunk in which you play (deliberately illegal) poker hands and stack Joker modifiers to beat escalating score targets.
community.consensus_summary: Balatro is one of the most acclaimed indie releases of the decade: Metacritic 90 from 32 critics (100% positive), OpenCritic 92 with 100% of critics recommending, and Steam shows about 97.8% positive across roughly 199k reviews (Overwhelmingly Positive). Critics compared it directly to Slay the Spire and called it extremely addictive and easy to pick up; players echo this and most of the negativity is about RNG-heavy high difficulties rather than the base game. It is not early access, but the long-promised 1.1 content update was delayed into 2026 (developer declined a 2025 date to avoid crunch), which some players read as the game being slow-moving or abandoned. It sold over 5 million copies by January 2025, and later won multiple awards (Game Developers Choice GOTY, Game Awards indie and debut categories, BAFTA Debut).
best_things: Extremely addictive 'one more run' loop: short runs, instant restarts, and big satisfying score cascades
Joker synergies and combo-building (retriggers, scaling jokers, Blueprint/DNA-style engines) create wildly different runs and 'broken build' payoffs
Easy to learn even for people who do not know poker; the run-info screen teaches hands visually and the game pulls in non-roguelike players
Juicy presentation: screen feel, animations, sound design and the chill, catchy soundtrack are repeatedly praised
Distinct pixel-art joker designs and overall CRT-like style give it a strong identity
Great value at about $15 with hundreds of hours of play for many, plus a huge unlock list (decks, vouchers, stakes) for completionists
Low system requirements and wide availability (PC, Mac, mobile, consoles); short runs suit mobile and handheld play
Made by one person, which reviewers and players treat as part of its appeal
worst_things: Luck dominates at higher stakes: players say skill matters less and run quality is decided by shop and joker RNG, with stacked RNG layers (shop, boss blinds, draws, probabilistic cards like Wheel of Fortune)
All-or-nothing blinds: missing a target by a hair ends the run, so losing is abrupt and feels bad rather than a slow, engaging struggle
Higher stakes remove resources (fewer discards, less income, stickers) which pushes players toward a narrow set of viable builds (high card, pairs) and away from straights and flushes
Some players find few meaningful decisions after the first few rounds once a build direction is locked in
Joker pool dilution as more jokers unlock: many weak or non-synergistic jokers clog shops, with no way to banish or curate them
Some find it designed to be compulsive rather than rewarding, leaving a flat or guilty feeling after wins
Progress does not sync between platforms (for example mobile and Steam), forcing players to unlock everything twice
Famously time-consuming: top Steam reviews joke about losing hours, 3 AM sessions and being unable to stop
improvements: Cross-platform progression sync (promised on a roadmap per Steam reviewers, still requested)
A way to curate the joker pool or banish unwanted jokers to fight dilution
Rework higher stakes and challenge decks so they demand skill and adaptation rather than more RNG and restarts
Reduce the grind of unlocking every stake on every deck (15 decks, many stakes)
More frequent content updates and communication about the delayed 1.1 update; the Matador joker and Blue Stake tweaks were previewed
Better balance of boss blinds, since a few are seen as run-killers with no time to pivot
unique_things: Takes poker hands as the combat system rather than fantasy combat, then breaks poker rules with jokers, so 'illegal poker' is the hook
Score is a chips-times-mult multiplication, so scaling comes from stacking multiplicative jokers into exponential numbers (players joke about e-notation scores)
Planet cards upgrade hand types, tarot and spectral cards edit the deck, so the deck itself is reshaped in play
Interest-based economy rewards saving money, creating constant spend-versus-save tension
Appeals to non-roguelike fans: reviewers called it a roguelike for people who do not like roguelikes
Cultural crossover reach: free Friends of Jimbo cosmetic packs (Witcher 3, Slay the Spire, Stardew Valley, etc.) and a cameo in a Black Mirror episode
tedious_or_disliked: Grinding stakes: players say one deck across all stakes, times 15 decks, means dozens of hours; one estimate cited 72 wins for the remaining decks' middle stakes
Gold Stake and above described as a slot-machine grind of rerolling the shop and restarting until a good joker appears
Restarting repeatedly on hard challenge decks when shops offer no scoring jokers early
100% completion and some achievements are seen as requiring RNG luck more than mastery
divisive_points: Whether higher stakes are satisfying challenge (risk and planning) or just RNG tedium; some love Gold Stake, others call it the game's weakest part
Is it deep strategy or a shallow dopamine machine? Critics praise layered systems while some Steam negatives call it not that deep
The addictive design: celebrated as pure fun by most, described as manipulative or guilt-inducing by a minority
Developer cadence: praised for avoiding crunch, but some players are frustrated by the delayed 1.1 update
community.reception_notes: Launched Feb 20, 2024 on PC and quickly became a breakout hit (over $1M in the first 8 hours and 1M copies in the first month, 5M+ by January 2025 per Wikipedia). Steam revenue estimator puts gross revenue at about $95M (Boxleiter-style estimate, not audited) and the Steam-owner estimate at 2-5M. Mobile launched Sept 2024 and Nintendo Switch 2 version Feb 2026; Metacritic platform scores are 90 (PC, PS5, Switch) and 95 (Xbox). Controversies: PEGI raised it to 18+ for gambling imagery (later appealed to 12+ in Feb 2025), and YouTube age-restricted many Balatro videos in March 2025. Patch 1.0.1c made the game easier. The promised 1.1 update slipped out of 2025 and the dev says it will be done when it is done. Steam page shows ongoing strong review scores through 2026.
